videos.title: How To Build A Jet Engine From Scratch
videos.description:
On November 21, 2026, Boom Supersonic (YC W16) fired its prototype engine core for the first time. In this episode of Hard Tech, YC’s Jared Friedman goes inside Boom’s Colorado Superpower Superfactory with founder and CEO Blake Scholl to see how they are building a jet engine from scratch.

The company is developing a shared core for two products: Superpower, a natural-gas turbine for AI data centers, and Symphony, the engine intended for the Overture supersonic airliner. Blake explains why Boom decided to build its own engine and its plan to use turbine revenue and operating data to help develop Overture.

On the factory floor, we explore in-house manufacturing, the challenge of making turbine blades survive extreme heat, and the custom software Boom uses to design and iterate on engine parts.

https://boomsupersonic.com

videos.title: 12 Rules for a Software Factory That Doesn't Ship Slop — Dex Horthy, Factory
videos.description:
The best model scores about 16% on Slop Code Bench, a new benchmark for how well agents evolve a code base over time. Dex Horthy uses that data to argue that software factories aren't new: they are good engineering with agents doing the building. He lays out 12 practices, from forward and back pressure to planning, visual alignment, lint rules against slop and a unified forge. Then he launches the Anti-Slop Manifesto and makes the case that reviewing work still matters.

Read the manifesto: https://slopmanifesto.com

- https://factory.ai

videos.title: The Revolution vs The Renaissance — Thariq Shihipar, OpenAI
videos.description:
At AI Engineer CODE, Thariq Shihipar revisits what he got wrong about coding agents, then asks what AI makes possible when people stay in the creative loop. He shows how the /human folder lets him tune a rock attack in his fighting game and explains why he stopped using the custom Mac Dock he built. We also get into decision models and who chooses which experiments get the compute.

Recorded at AI Engineer CODE. Thariq announced that he had joined OpenAI after the interview.
